body:
Reply with plain text only, no JSON, no preamble, and do not send messages to anyone else. Do not ask questions; decide.

You are drafting the lines of short scenes for a Halloween D&D video game, "The Crooked Moon", a folk-horror campaign set in Wickermoor Hollow, a haunted valley of endless night under a giant Crooked Moon with a crone's face. The look is a Halloween that never ends, drawn like an 1980s cartoon. The player controls a party of four. A scene happens inside the Crooked House, a haunted manor on a hill above the village, while a storm has shut the party in.

Each scene is a "Thread of Fate" opening beat (an Incitement) for one party companion. It plays automatically as the party steps into a room. It is made of two kinds of lines:
- NARRATOR lines: spoken by the Vagrant, the green-skinned ferryman of the ghost train, who tells the tale afterwards in a folksy Southern drawl. In this house his humour is gone: hushed, dry and dead level, the drawl stripped to bare bones, never a joke, never a gloat. He may use the companion's name in the third person. Present tense, one or two sentences, under about 32 words each. Concrete senses (a smell, a sound, a touch) over adjectives. Never tell the player what to feel. Never "suddenly". No game words (no HP, roll, check, level, save, class names). No facts beyond those given. Drop a final g ("hangin'") in about one Narrator line in three, no other dialect spelling.
- INTERJECT lines: the companion's own spoken words, one or two short sentences, under about 28 words, in the companion's voice sheet given below, using their pet phrases sparingly (at most one per scene) and not repeating their existing lines.

Rules for all lines: plain punctuation only (commas, full stops, hyphens, apostrophes, quotation marks); no em dashes, no semicolons, no brackets, no backticks, no stage directions, no placeholders. Do not invent new people, places, monsters or history beyond the facts given. Our own words; nothing quoted from any book.

OUTPUT FORMAT, nothing else. For each node give lines in order, one per row, exactly like

NODE start
NARRATOR: the line
INTERJECT: the line
NARRATOR: the line
INTERJECT: the line

NODE opt1
NARRATOR: the line
INTERJECT: the line
INSPIRE: four to seven words, past tense, with no name, saying what the companion did (for example: read a dead clerk's warning)

(and so on for opt2 and opt3.) The "start" node has exactly four rows in the order shown. Each option node has exactly one NARRATOR, one INTERJECT and one INSPIRE row.
THE COMPANION: TOBIN HAYWARD, a Harvestborn (living scarecrow, straw and burlap) Druid, a pragmatic rural diagnostician of curses and rot. Burlap thumbs, straw ribs, little field mice in his lapels, stiff pruning knife. Brisk and unsentimental, fussy, afraid of open flame (a spark would burn his straw and the dried wedding flowers braided in his chest). His secret (never state it): in a famine he burned a neighbour's blighted orchard to save his own.
HIS VOICE: brisk diagnostic sentences in tidy counted rhythms that stop on a dry two-beat pause; gentle farmhand's country drawl; orchard, grafting, blight, soil, timber and stitching words. Pet phrases: "tie off the rot" (once a scene at most), "good soil, bad seed", "hold still now". Calls the Crooked Man "the crooked spindle-man". Under stress his words crowd together. His existing lines (do not repeat): "Hold still, you're fraying at the cuff and your pulse is skipping every fourth beat." / "Keep that lantern back, two paces back, I am dry straw from collar to heel." / "Dirt round here tastes of sour turnip and third-rate hexing."

THE SCENE (the Conservatory, glass walls and glass roof, rain hammering, dead vines, benches, and one vivid living bergamot tree with hard green fruit; a woman in black sits still on a bench facing it). Tobin steps past the dead vines, presses a burlap thumb to the tree's weeping bark and jerks his hand back as if the sap scalded him. In the tree he sees black rot split the trunk and run out across the valley toward a hill crawling with pale centipedes, and a phantom smell of scorching apple-wood sets the mice squeaking and diving for his pockets. He pulls three straws from his ribs, twists a stiff splint round a cracked bergamot twig, and clears his throat hard to cover the shake in his fingers.
SIGNATURE LINE (use it verbatim as the FIRST INTERJECT of the start node): "Bark's cold, nothing burning here, only a deep sour canker running down the taproot toward that centipede hill."
NODE start: Narrator describes the thumb on the bark and the jerked-back hand and the weeping sap; the signature interject; Narrator describes the smell of scorching apple-wood, the mice, the splint and the shaking fingers; a second interject, Tobin steadying himself with a diagnosis.
THE THREE OPTIONS and what each means for Tobin:
opt1 "What did that tree just show you?" => he steadies and commits to tracking the rot to its source.
opt2 "Your hand shook. Did the sap burn you?" => he feels seen past the mask and admits, without detail, that the rot reminds him of an old orchard fire.
opt3 "Leave the tree. We have a manor to clear." => he pockets his pruning knife and keeps the diagnosis to himself; the quiet way on.
Each option node is the aftermath: the Narrator line shows what Tobin does with his hands (splint, mice, knife, straw); the interject is his voice answering the party.
result:
NODE start
NARRATOR: Rain drums hard on the glass roof while Tobin steps past the dead vines and presses his burlap thumb to the weeping bergamot bark. He jerks his hand back fast.
INTERJECT: Bark's cold, nothing burning here, only a deep sour canker running down the taproot toward that centipede hill.
NARRATOR: A smell of scorchin' apple-wood fills the damp air, sendin' his lapel mice squeakin' into his pockets. He pulls three straws from his ribs, splints a cracked twig, and clears his throat.
INTERJECT: Split's clean through the cambium, four inches wide, weeping black pitch into the loam. It needs a sharp blade.

NODE opt1
NARRATOR: Tobin pulls his stiff pruning knife and tests the flat of the blade against his burlap thumb, steadying his grip.
INTERJECT: Blight does not stop at the fence line when the rootstock is sour. We track that seam down the valley and tie off the rot.
INSPIRE: vowed to trace the valley blight

NODE opt2
NARRATOR: He tucks the loose straw back between his ribs and strokes a trembling mouse through the cloth of his pocket.
INTERJECT: Sap's cold as well-water, just caught a whiff of old orchard smoke in the grain. Good soil, bad seed.
INSPIRE: named the smell of old smoke

NODE opt3
NARRATOR: Tobin folds his pruning knife shut with a dry click, slides it into his coat, and dusts the damp bark from his knuckles.
INTERJECT: Aye, the splint will hold the bough till morning. Keep your boots off the surface roots as we go.
INSPIRE: splinted the bough and moved on
